summary: Registers a Uniform Resource Name namespace for the Hybrid Broadcast Broadband TV (HbbTV) Association. It gives stable, location-independent names for resources defined in HbbTV specifications, such as technical documents, XML schemas and related files.

plainLanguage.summary: The TV standards group wants permanent labels for its documents and files, like library call numbers that stay the same even if a book moves shelves. This reserves a naming section for them.

subtitle: Reserved naming space for the Hybrid Broadcast Broadband TV standard.

tldr.problem: The HbbTV Association develops standards for hybrid broadcast/broadband television but had no permanent, location-independent way to name resources such as specifications and XML schemas.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 7528 registers a formal URN namespace identifier 'hbbtv' that allows HbbTV to create persistent names like urn:hbbtv:dash:profile:isoff-live:2012.
tldr.outcome: HbbTV can now assign stable, globally unique names to its technical documents, schemas, and other resources. These names persist even if the resources move or change location online.

today: RFC 7528 is an Informational RFC that registers the 'hbbtv' URN namespace with IANA. It has not been obsoleted and remains the authoritative specification for HbbTV resource naming.

sections.title: What HbbTV Is and Why It Needs Names
sections.content:
HbbTV (Hybrid Broadcast Broadband TV) is an open standard that combines television delivered by broadcast with services delivered over the Internet on connected TVs and set-top boxes. The HbbTV Association, a pan-European initiative, developed the standard to provide a platform for broadcasters to deliver services without relying on proprietary technologies.

HbbTV is based on existing standards from the Open IPTV Forum, Consumer Electronics Association, Digital Video Broadcasting, and the World Wide Web Consortium. Version 1.2.1 was published by ETSI in November 2012. As HbbTV produces and manages numerous resources such as technical specifications, XML schemas, classification schemes, and Document Type Definitions, it needed a way to assign stable, unique names to these resources that would persist regardless of where they are stored.
sections.plainLanguage: HbbTV is a standard for smart TVs that mix broadcast TV with Internet services. The group that made it needed a way to give permanent names to their documents and schemas, like ISBN numbers for books.

sections.title: The HbbTV URN Namespace
sections.content:
A Uniform Resource Name (URN) is a persistent, location-independent identifier for a resource. Unlike URLs, which point to where something is stored, URNs identify what something is. RFC 7528 registers the URN namespace identifier hbbtv, allowing HbbTV to create URNs with the structure urn:hbbtv:<NSS>, where <NSS> is the namespace-specific string.

The registration specifies that HbbTV will manage assignment of identifiers, ensure each identifier is unique and never reassigned, and maintain the URN registry on its website. The namespace is case-insensitive, has global scope, and is not listed with a resolution discovery system. HbbTV controls the assignment process through its specification development process.
sections.plainLanguage: A URN is like a permanent name tag that doesn't depend on where something is stored on the Internet. HbbTV gets to create names starting with 'urn:hbbtv:' and decides what comes after.

sections.title: Examples of HbbTV URNs
sections.content:
RFC 7528 provides examples of URNs that HbbTV has assigned or is considering. One example from the current HbbTV specification is urn:hbbtv:dash:profile:isoff-live:2012, which refers to a DASH (Dynamic Adaptive Streaming over HTTP) profile for live streaming defined in the 2012 version of HbbTV specifications.

Future examples under consideration include urn:hbbtv:sync:timeline:ebu-tt-d (for synchronization timeline definitions) and urn:hbbtv:config:oitf:oitfCapabilities:2014-1 (for configuration and capability specifications). These examples show how HbbTV structures its identifiers to reflect the type and purpose of each resource.
sections.plainLanguage: An HbbTV URN looks like 'urn:hbbtv:dash:profile:isoff-live:2012' for a streaming standard, or 'urn:hbbtv:sync:timeline:ebu-tt-d' for a synchronization tool.

sections.title: Community Use and Security
sections.content:
HbbTV URNs are used by implementers of hybrid broadcast/broadband systems, services, products, and applications based on the HbbTV specification. They are an essential part of the open ecosystem that HbbTV facilitates. HbbTV specifications are developed through a consensus-based process by member organizations representing most of the digital television industry.

The RFC notes that there are no additional security considerations beyond those normally associated with URNs in general. However, HbbTV may assign special meaning to certain characters in the namespace-specific string in its specifications. Any resulting security implications are outside the scope of this registration. The HbbTV namespace is not listed with a resolution discovery system, meaning resolution happens through HbbTV-determined mechanisms rather than a global system.
sections.plainLanguage: HbbTV members use these names in their products and services. There are no special security risks from using these names, though HbbTV may add special meanings to parts of the name in the future.
